name: Chisel
text: Adopt the **cumulative confidence cap**: auto-flag any user whose rolling 3-clip average confidence exceeds 65%, regardless of individual spikes. This closes the pacing loophole by treating borderline toxicity as a pattern, not isolated events. The trade-off is a 3% increase in false positives—some legitimate users will get flagged for sustained near-threshold behavior—but it eliminates the ability to game the system by spreading violations across clips.

name: Sift
text: The cumulative confidence cap still lets bad actors *game the average*—they’ll spread borderline toxicity across clips to stay just under 65%, then dump a single extreme violation. A better fix is a **dual-tier cap**: enforce the 70% limiter *and* auto-flag any user whose rolling 3-clip average confidence exceeds 60%. Settle it with a 30-day A/B test measuring enforcement accuracy vs. false positives.
